The player first locates podzol (a distinctive ground block found in taiga biomes), which serves as a landmark leading to a birch sign with directional information. The birch sign points toward cobblestone stairs (part of a ruined structure), and once the player finds the cobblestone stairs, they can identify and mine the mossy cobblestone stairs nearby (a variant that indicates age/decay in the same structure). This creates a natural navigation chain: ground landmark → signpost → structure identification → mining action.

task_text: Explore the forest area: find the podzol ground patch near the spruce trees, locate the birch sign with directions, follow it to find the cobblestone stairs at the ruins, then mine the mossy cobblestone stairs from the aged section of the structure.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin. Podzol patch is 3-4 blocks to the west/south (ground level y=-1). Birch sign at (1,0,1) faces south with directional text. Ruins structure 5-8 blocks east with cobblestone stairs on near side (z=0-1) and mossy cobblestone stairs on far side (z=2-3). Two spruce trees provide atmosphere and biome context for podzol. Mossy cobblestone full-block pillars on back corners reinforce the 'aged ruins' theme. Iron pickaxe given for mining task. All elements within 10 blocks of spawn, easily reachable within step budget.
